recommendation: Keep the core audit commit as-is. If OO wants the applied FHIR-41414 wording reflected exactly in the active SupplyDelivery artifact, update HL7/oo-incubator input/resources/supplydelivery/StructureDefinition-SupplyDelivery.xml so SupplyDelivery.subject says person, group, or organization.
issue_request: FHIR-41414 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6. It requested changing SupplyDelivery.patient to SupplyDelivery.subject with Patient, Group, and Organization targets; keeping the patient search parameter restricted to Patient; adding a subject search parameter; adding Group to receiver; updating Patient and Group compartments; and adding the family/household-only Group comment to subject and receiver.
initial_application: Core commits 30a4512bff and 53854dc11c applied the issue before this reconciliation: the first changed the SupplyDelivery structure definition, search parameter bundle, and compartments; the second added target Patient to SupplyDelivery-patient after Jira feedback that Group and Organization should not be advertised for the patient search parameter.
additional_context: Commit 3b38b80cf2 later removed SupplyDelivery and neighboring OO resources from active core configuration and compartments, and current core module pages link SupplyDelivery to https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/oo-incubator/. The external OO incubator artifact has the requested subject/receiver targets, comments, and search parameters, but its SupplyDelivery.subject definition still uses the older person-only wording, so any remaining exact-definition cleanup belongs in HL7/oo-incubator rather than this core checkout.
reconciliation: No core source files were changed. The published commit is an empty audit recording that FHIR core no longer owns an active built SupplyDelivery definition to edit.
